subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Find the sum of all 4-digit numbers that can be formed using the digits 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (no digit repeated).

mark_split.label: How often each digit sits in each place

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the sum of all these four-digit numbers — how often a digit appears in a place, what each place contributes, and how you finish.
insider_note: The number the whole sum is built on is 24: each digit sits in each place ⁴P₃ = 24 times, while ⁵P₄ = 120 counts the numbers themselves. The sum is 24 · 25 · 1111, and the digit sum is 25, not 24.

steps.label: How often a digit sits in each place
steps.margin_note: First mark. Put 9 in the units place; the other three places take the remaining 4 digits in ⁴P₃ = 24 ways. The same is true for every digit and every place.
steps.memory_tip: Fix one digit in a place; the other three places take ⁴P₃ = 24 ways. 24 is the appearances, 120 is the numbers.
lines: Fix one digit in the units place: the other
three places are filled in ⁴P₃ = 24 ways.
So each digit sits in each place 24 times.

recall.must_convey: That with one digit fixed in a place the other three places are filled in 4 P 3 = 24 ways, so every digit appears 24 times in every place.

each digit appears twenty four times in each place
four P three is twenty four arrangements for the other three places

every digit sits in every place twenty four times

steps.why: Adding 120 numbers one by one is not possible in an exam. The place-by-place method works because the count 24 is the same for every digit in every place, so the sum can be built from place values.
common_mistakes: Using ⁵P₄ = 120 as the number of times a digit appears — that is the number of numbers, not the appearances of one digit in one place.
Using ³P₃ = 6 for the remaining places; four digits remain after one is fixed.

steps.label: Contribution of each place value
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The units place holds each digit 24 times, so it contributes 24 × (1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9) × 1. The tens place contributes the same × 10, and so on. Collect the place values as 1111.
steps.memory_tip: The digit sum is 25, not 24. Collect the place values as 1000 + 100 + 10 + 1 = 1111.
lines: Tens place contributes 24 · 25 · 10, and so on.

recall.must_convey: That each place contributes 24 times the digit sum 25 times its place value, and the four places together give 24 × 25 × 1111.
accept: sum of digits is twenty five, each place gives twenty four times twenty five times its place value, together twenty four times twenty five times one one one one
the units, tens, hundreds and thousands add up to one thousand one hundred and eleven times twenty four times twenty five
twenty four into twenty five into one one one one
digits sum twenty five, prathi place twenty four into twenty five into place value, total eleven eleven tho multiply
six hundred times one thousand one hundred eleven

steps.why: A number is its digits times their place values, so the sum of all the numbers is the sum of all the digit-appearances times place values. Grouping by place turns 120 additions into one product.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by 1111 but forgetting the 24 — each digit appears 24 times, not once.
Using 11111 (five places) — the numbers have four digits.
Taking the digit sum as 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 24 by slip; it is 25.

steps.label: Add the place contributions
steps.memory_tip: 600 × 1111 = 6,66,600. Check it as 6 × 1111 = 6666 with two zeros added.

recall.must_convey: That the product 600 times 1111 is evaluated to 666600.

steps.why: The last step is only arithmetic, but the examiner marks the number. 600 × 1111 = 666600 can be checked as 6 × 1111 = 6666 followed by two zeros.
common_mistakes: Writing 66,660 or 6,66,000 by dropping a digit.
Leaving the answer as 24 × 25 × 1111 without evaluating it.
